original.title: Writing a Professional Email that Respects Workplace Culture
original.body_en:
✍️ Writing Task

Title: Writing a Professional Email that Respects Workplace Culture
Time: 1–2 hours
Objective: Practice adapting your written communication to U.S. business etiquette by showing respect, clarity, and professionalism.

Scenario:

You've started your first week at a U.S. company. On Tuesday, your manager, Alex Johnson, gave you a project task. The instructions were clear at the time, but now you realize you are missing one important detail. Instead of guessing, you decide to write a short, professional email to clarify the task.

Your Task:

Write a professional email (100–150 words) to your manager, Alex Johnson. Your email should:

Use a clear subject line.

Begin with a respectful greeting.

Explain what you need clarification on—politely and directly.

Show appreciation for their time and guidance.

End with a professional sign-off.

Why This Matters:

In U.S. workplaces, asking for clarification is seen as responsible and professional, not as weakness. Writing this way shows:

💬 Clarity → You know how to state your need directly.

🎯 Tone → You respect your manager's time.

🚀 Confidence → You own your role and ask questions to succeed.

Example Email:

Subject: Clarification on Project Task

Hi Alex,

Thank you again for outlining the project details on Tuesday. I want to make sure I'm completing the task correctly. Could you confirm the specific data source I should use for the analysis?

I appreciate your time and guidance—I just want to ensure I deliver the work in line with your expectations.

Best regards,
Daniela

👉 Your Turn: Write your own email in your notes or course journal. Then, read it out loud to check for clarity and tone.

original.body_es:
✍️ Tarea de Escritura

Título: Escribir un Correo Electrónico Profesional que Respete la Cultura Laboral
Tiempo: 1–2 horas
Objetivo: Practicar la adaptación de tu comunicación escrita a la etiqueta empresarial de EE.UU. mostrando respeto, claridad y profesionalismo.

Escenario:

Has comenzado tu primera semana en una empresa de EE.UU. El martes, tu gerente, Alex Johnson, te dio una tarea de proyecto. Las instrucciones fueron claras en ese momento, pero ahora te das cuenta de que te falta un detalle importante. En lugar de adivinar, decides escribir un correo electrónico corto y profesional para aclarar la tarea.

Tu Tarea:

Escribe un correo electrónico profesional (100–150 palabras) a tu gerente, Alex Johnson. Tu correo debe:

Usar una línea de asunto clara.

Comenzar con un saludo respetuoso.

Explicar sobre qué necesitas aclaración—de manera educada y directa.

Mostrar agradecimiento por su tiempo y orientación.

Terminar con una despedida profesional.

Por Qué Esto Importa:

En los lugares de trabajo de EE.UU., pedir aclaraciones se considera responsable y profesional, no una debilidad. Escribir de esta manera muestra:

💬 Claridad → Sabes cómo expresar tu necesidad directamente.

🎯 Tono → Respetas el tiempo de tu gerente.

🚀 Confianza → Asumes tu rol y haces preguntas para tener éxito.

Correo Electrónico de Ejemplo:

Asunto: Clarification on Project Task

Hi Alex,

Thank you again for outlining the project details on Tuesday. I want to make sure I'm completing the task correctly. Could you confirm the specific data source I should use for the analysis?

I appreciate your time and guidance—I just want to ensure I deliver the work in line with your expectations.

Best regards,
Daniela

👉 Tu Turno: Escribe tu propio correo en tus notas o diario del curso. Luego, léelo en voz alta para verificar la claridad y el tono.
